name: 993/993 Turbo connecting rod, Ti64 bionic load-path shank F0 concept (PicoGK)
picogk_enhancement: Bionic: the shank between the eyes is grown by 3D SIMP topology optimisation (bionic.json, topopt.py) for four stated load cases: 111.8 kN compression and 17.6 kN inertia tension from the engineering screen, 3.2 kN in-plane whip and 2.2 kN out-of-plane load at the small end, big-end bore fixed; PicoGK smooths the density into organic members and fuses the exact bores, eye rings, bolt lugs and bolt passages. The cap split is not modelled (body and cap one piece). Loads are synthetic screening values, not measurements.

piston_pin_diameter_mm.note: published pin size, used as nominal small-end bore without clearance

big_end_od_mm.note: F0 hypothesis from connecting_rod.py; bionic: design-domain width, the fixed housing ring is 67 mm OD (4.5 mm wall)

small_end_od_mm.note: F0 hypothesis from connecting_rod.py; bionic: the fixed eye is 31 mm OD (4 mm wall), the optimiser adds around it

bolt_clearance_diameter_mm.note: concept bolt passage; ARP 2000 family published, size not

small_end_oil_hole_mm.note: small-end oil drilling, not in the concept

rod_length_envelope_mm.note: bionic design domain x -42..148 (big-end OD to small-end OD of the F0 rod)

rod_width_envelope_mm.note: bionic design domain y +/-42 (big-end OD 78 mm and bolt lugs)

open_interfaces: bearing shells, crankpin and big-end fit
cap joint, bolt size, seats and preload
cap split line and fracture-split process (not modelled in the bionic body)
status: F0 concept geometry - not fitted, not tested, not safe, not released, not a print file; prohibited pending engineering, never to be installed in an engine
